title: a method that assigns its name more than once returns one value, and a call in a loop leaves the stack as it found it
note: IEC 61131-3, methods: the value of the method is the last assignment to its name before it returns; the caller sees exactly one value, and a method that never assigns returns the default of its type (0); Pick(i) is i up to 5, 2 i for 6 to 8 and -i for 9 and 10: 15 + 42 - 19 = 38; the loop makes ten calls, the call as a statement an eleventh, Never() adds 100
